message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “UNO.” | | **Setup** | Shuffle a standard Uno deck (108 cards). Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the value of the top discard. If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile until you find one you can play. | | **Special cards** | • **+2** – Next player draws two and skips a turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **+4 Wild** – You choose the next color and the next player draws four (must be challenged if you suspect you could have played another card). | | **Winning a round** | When a player discards all their cards they win the round. Opponents tally the point values of the cards still in their hands (number cards = face value, +2/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/+4 = 50). Those points are added to the winner’s score. | | **Game end** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon total (usually 500) wins the game. | That’s the core of Uno—simple, fast, and full of surprises!
